title: High-touch Customer Intake Orchestrator and Prioritization Heuristic
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: High-touch customer requests (strategic pilots, SLA escalations, custom routing) lack a single, consistent intake and prioritization flow. As a result, PMs and Eng ops make ad-hoc decisions, tickets slip past roadmap planning cycles, and we lose visibility into which asks should drive product work versus partner engineering or account work.

Goal: Build a standardized 'Intake Orchestrator' for high-touch requests that: (1) captures consistent signals, (2) computes a prioritized score for roadmap consideration, (3) surfaces automation and routing rules for CS/Sales/Support, and (4) integrates into our cycle planning and OKR tracking. This should reduce ad-hoc escalations, shorten decision latency, and align top-account asks with measurable outcomes.

Scope: MVP covers commercial accounts (ARR > $100k) and strategic pilots. Excludes low-touch self-serve feature requests handled by the community portal. Deliverables: intake form + webhook, scoring heuristic service (configurable weights), Linear auto-tagging + priority suggestions, a dashboard for roadmap triage, playbook for escalation SLAs and owner handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form implemented and accessible to CS/Sales/Solutions Eng with required fields
Automated score computed on submission and visible as a Linear field
Triage dashboard shows all active high-touch items with score, owner, and SLAs
Pilot run with 5 strategic accounts and collection of 90-day outcome metrics
Defined routing rules documented and adopted by CS/Sales playbooks
related_metrics: Decision latency: median days from intake to roadmap decision
Percent of high-touch requests routed to product vs. account work
Number of escalations avoided by automation
rollout_plan: Week 1: Design intake form + scoring signals with CS and Sales
Week 2: Build form, webhooks, and Linear integration + prototype dashboard
Week 3: Internal pilot with Solutions Eng and 2 accounts; collect feedback
Week 4-6: Iterate scoring weights, add automation for routing, finalize playbooks
Week 7: Wider pilot with 5 accounts and present to Roadmap Council for Q2 commitments
risks_and_tradeoffs: Overfitting weights to initial pilot accounts could bias prioritization against smaller but strategic segments
Automating routing too aggressively may bypass human judgment needed for nuanced security or compliance asks
Building a heavyweight scoring engine delays time-to-value versus a lightweight checklist approach
